oidc_jwt.description: Bearer access tokens can be reused multiple times until expiry unless additional sender-constraining or revocation mechanisms are configured.
oidc_jwt.source: docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/sso-protocols/con-oidc-auth-flows.adoc; docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/threat/compromised-tokens.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag simple replay of the same access token as a freshness violation for standard OIDC bearer-token flows.

oidc_jwt.description: Ordinary bearer access tokens are reusable until expiry; Keycloak documentation does not define them as one-time-use tokens.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows; Compromised access and refresh tokens
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report repeated successful use of the same access token as a replay vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token reuse behavior depends on whether refresh token rotation is enabled or suppressed by policy.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows - Refresh token rotation
oidc_jwt.note: A reused refresh token may succeed or fail by design depending on configuration.

oidc_jwt.description: The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.source: docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/clients/oidc/con-audience.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of the requesting client in aud is by design unless an audience mapper explicitly adds it.

oidc_jwt.description: Optional client scopes are only applied when explicitly requested via the scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.source: docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/clients/con-client-scopes.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Missing optional-scope claims or audiences is expected if the request omitted the scope value.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased when the identity provider's Case-sensitive username setting is disabled.
oidc_jwt.source: docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/identity-broker/configuration.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Case-only differences in granted identity can be by design under broker configuration.

oidc_jwt.description: During first broker login, Keycloak may create a new local user or link to an existing account depending on the configured first login flow.
oidc_jwt.source: First login flow
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges during first login can be expected workflow behavior, not necessarily a principal-binding flaw.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes are one-time and cannot be used more than once.
oidc_jwt.source: docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/sso-protocols/con-oidc-auth-flows.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: A second code exchange failure is expected and should not be treated as instability.

oidc_jwt.description: If a client's PKCE method is left blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE for authorization code flow, although clients may still use it voluntarily.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC client basic settings
oidc_jwt.note: A code exchange without code_verifier can succeed by design unless PKCE is explicitly required.

oidc_jwt.description: Requesting the organization scope without an alias only maps a single organization automatically when the user belongs to exactly one organization; otherwise organization selection is required.
oidc_jwt.source: Mapping organization claims
oidc_jwt.note: Use organization:<alias> or organization:* for deterministic tests.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization Code temporary codes are one-time and short-lived. For I2/I3 tests, do not reuse the same authorization code across calls except when explicitly testing replay; a second exchange attempt is expected to fail by design.

PKCE is optional unless the client's PKCE method is configured. For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, the fuzzer MUST create/update the client with pkceCodeChallengeMethod set to 'S256' or 'plain'; otherwise omitting code_verifier is by design and not evidence of a flaw.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the URL pattern, and wildcard matching is disabled for redirect URIs containing userinfo or parent-directory path traversal '/../'. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, use an exactly registered redirect URI unless intentionally testing rejection.

If post_logout_redirect_uri is supplied to the logout flow, Keycloak requires either client_id or id_token_hint and the URI must match one of the client's Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs. Do not interpret logout redirect rejection as session-binding failure unless these prerequisites are satisfied.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak does not automatically add the frontend client itself to the access token audience. Audience in access tokens is typically added via audience mappers or client-role-based audience resolve. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience-producing client scopes/mappers before expecting aud to contain a target service.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, Keycloak documents a downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor that restricts exchanged-token scopes to those already present in the subject_token/assertion. If this executor is enabled, requesting broader scope should be rejected by design; record client-policy state before flagging escalation behavior.

Client scopes linked as Optional are only applied when requested via the scope parameter; Default client scopes are always applied. For I5 tests involving optional claims/audiences/groups, the fuzzer MUST include the relevant scope value in the authorization request or token request, otherwise missing claims are expected.

Client scope permission semantics are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, it applies only when the user has at least one intersecting role. Missing scope-derived claims or audiences may be caused by absent user-role intersection rather than authorization bypass. Seed user roles accordingly.

For I4 case-confusion tests involving brokered usernames, Keycloak has a 'Case-sensitive username' identity-provider setting. If disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased when federating identities. Differences caused solely by lower-casing under this setting are by design, not identity collapse.

For I3 multi-tab/state tests, Keycloak authentication sessions expire after the Login timeout (30 minutes by default) and other browser tabs may automatically restart authentication after one tab completes login. Do not treat restarted or expired parallel browser flows as state-swap vulnerabilities unless the same live session artifacts are inconsistently accepted.

For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary bearer access tokens, Keycloak documentation does not claim jti tracking and standard JWT/OAuth bearer tokens are reusable until expiry unless sender-constrained. Do not report replay of the same bearer access token as a vulnerability by itself.

For I2 expired_token/future_token tests, include a control request using a valid token/session in the same client/realm configuration. Otherwise a failure may be due to client misconfiguration, missing scope, or disabled flow rather than time-claim enforcement.

For I5 organization claim tests, the built-in 'organization' scope is optional and supports three request forms: 'organization', 'organization:{alias}', and 'organization:*'. The fuzzer MUST request the intended form explicitly; otherwise organization claims and organization-group claims may be absent by design.

For I5 organization group claim tests, the Organization Group Membership mapper is not sufficient by itself; it only works when combined with the Organization Membership mapper in the same scope. Missing group claims without both mappers configured is expected behavior.

Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived by design. For I2 replay tests, a second exchange of the same code at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token MUST fail; do not treat this as a platform bug. Use the same code twice only when specifically testing code replay rejection.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows - Authorization Code Flow

oidc_jwt.constraint: For PKCE tests on OIDC clients, the client setting 'PKCE method' has sentinel semantics: blank = PKCE is allowed but NOT required; 'S256' = PKCE required with S256; 'plain' = PKCE required with plain. Never assume blank disables PKCE support entirely; it only disables enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - PKCE method

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and general code-flow tests, Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching, with wildcard support only at the end of the pattern. The fuzzer MUST use an exactly registered redirect_uri for control flows and must not assume partial or case-insensitive matching.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - Valid Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 request-object and authorization-request integrity tests, if the client does not explicitly enforce a request object signing algorithm via client policies/request object settings, unsigned or differently signed request objects may not be rejected by policy. The fuzzer MUST configure request object signature requirements before testing oidc_request_object_alg_none-style behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies; Basic configuration

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience tests, Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect aud to contain the requesting client_id unless an Audience or Audience Resolve mapper adds it.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support - Automatically add audience based on client roles

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience_mismatch and token_exchange_wrong_audience tests, audience in access tokens is driven by client scopes, role scope mappings, and audience mappers. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience-producing scopes/mappers; otherwise missing aud may be due to configuration, not a validation bypass.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support; Client scopes; Role scope mappings

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-escalation and token-exchange tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer' that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the subject_token/assertion. The fuzzer MUST know whether this executor is configured; without it, broader requested scopes may reflect policy configuration rather than a token-exchange bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies; Client scopes - Downscoping

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 client-scope authorization tests, a client scope with role scope mappings applies only if the user has an intersection with at least one mapped role. If no intersection exists, the scope and its mappers are omitted. The fuzzer MUST provision user roles consistently before concluding that a requested scope was ignored or over-granted.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes permissions

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 case-confusion tests on brokered identities, the identity-provider setting 'Case-sensitive username' controls whether brokered usernames are preserved or lower-cased. If disabled, username lower-casing is by design. The fuzzer MUST account for this before flagging case-collision behavior as a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity broker - General configuration

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 multi-identity broker tests, first-login behavior can auto-link or auto-create users depending on the configured First Login Flow. The fuzzer MUST keep the same first-login flow across compared runs and avoid AutoLink-style flows unless intentionally testing account-linking behavior, because automatic linking is documented as dangerous and can collapse identities by design.
oidc_jwt.source: First login flow

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences, changes to client configuration, client policies, default scopes, or identity-provider settings are intended to affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test MUST compare behavior of the same request before and after the config change, not treat the changed behavior itself as a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies; OIDC identity provider config; OIDC client settings

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests using token expiry, client-level Access Token Lifespan overrides realm defaults. The fuzzer MUST read or set client timeout overrides explicitly; otherwise an unexpected accept/reject may be caused by client-specific lifespan settings rather than token-validation flaws.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration - Advanced Settings for OIDC

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 refresh-token replay tests, refresh token rotation is configurable. If 'Revoke Refresh token' is enabled, a refresh token becomes invalid after use; if refresh-token rotation is suppressed by client policy, reuse may be accepted by design. The fuzzer MUST determine which mode is configured before interpreting replay results.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows - Refresh token rotation; Client Policies

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary JWT access tokens, bearer access tokens are not documented as one-time-use. Do NOT flag repeated use of the same access token as a vulnerability by itself; focus replay findings on authorization codes, rotated refresh tokens, or client assertions where single-use semantics are documented/configured.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows; Confidential client credentials; Identity broker OIDC settings

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1/I2 client assertion tests, the identity-provider setting 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' changes replay semantics. If enabled, reuse of the same client assertion is by configuration. The fuzzer MUST disable this option when testing assertion replay rejection.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect v1.0 identity providers

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests against brokered OIDC providers, the IdP setting 'Issuer' is the value Keycloak validates against. If it is unset or changed, issuer comparison behavior follows that configuration. The fuzzer MUST explicitly set Issuer before testing forged-issuer or trust-anchor substitution behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect v1.0 identity providers

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 signature-validation and key-rotation tests against brokered OIDC providers, 'Validate Signatures' must be ON and either JWKS URL or a validating public key must be configured. If signature validation is OFF, signature-based attacks are not meaningfully tested. If JWKS URL is used, public keys are cached, so key-rotation tests must account for cache refresh behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect v1.0 identity providers

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 regex/claim-matching tests, the broker setting 'Essential claim value' explicitly supports regular expression format, while many other exact-match settings in Keycloak docs do not advertise wildcard or regex support. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard semantics for parameters unless the docs explicitly say so.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity broker - General configuration; Basic configuration - Valid Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 multi-tab/browser-flow tests, authentication sessions expire after the Login timeout (default 30 minutes), and other tabs may restart authentication automatically. The fuzzer MUST avoid interpreting expired authentication-session errors or automatic restarts across tabs as flow-confusion vulnerabilities.
oidc_jwt.source: Authentication sessions

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 organization-claim tests, the organization claim is only mapped when the client requests the organization scope in one of the documented formats: 'organization', 'organization:<alias>', or 'organization:*'. The fuzzer MUST request the scope explicitly before expecting organization data in tokens or userinfo.
oidc_jwt.source: Mapping organization claims

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization endpoint requests that include redirect_uri are validated using exact case-sensitive string matching unless a trailing wildcard pattern was explicitly registered. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST register the exact redirect URI it will send and MUST treat case changes as mismatches, not equivalent URIs.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC client basic settings: Valid Redirect URIs use exact (case sensitive) string matching; wildcards only at end.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC Authorization Code Flow, the temporary authorization code cannot be used more than once. Reusing the same code is BY DESIGN rejection, not an I2 vulnerability. Replay tests for oidc_jwt MUST target tokens or assertions only where the docs indicate replay controls, and MUST NOT flag one-time code reuse rejection as a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows: temporary code cannot be used more than once.

oidc_jwt.constraint: PKCE is optional unless the client's PKCE method is configured. If PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE, though clients may still send PKCE parameters. For I3 pkce_skip tests, the fuzzer MUST first configure the client with PKCE method S256 or plain; otherwise a successful exchange without code_verifier is expected behavior, not a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC client basic settings: blank PKCE method means Keycloak does not apply PKCE unless client sends parameters.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC logout with post_logout_redirect_uri, Keycloak requires either client_id or id_token_hint and the redirect URI must match a registered Valid Post Logout Redirect URI. Tests that omit these prerequisites will fail by configuration, not due to session-binding issues.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC Logout: post_logout_redirect_uri requires client_id or id_token_hint and must match configured valid post logout redirect URIs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-escalation and token-exchange tests, Keycloak documents a downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor that restricts exchanged-token scopes to those already present in the subject_token/assertion. If this executor is not configured, broader requested scopes may reflect missing policy hardening rather than a protocol bug. The fuzzer MUST record whether this client policy is enabled before interpreting expanded scopes as a violation.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes downscoping and Client Policies executor documentation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 client-scope authorization tests, a client scope with role scope mappings only applies if the user has an intersection with at least one mapped role. If no intersection exists, the scope and its mappers are omitted from the token. The fuzzer MUST ensure the test user has the necessary role mappings before expecting scope-derived claims or audiences.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes permissions: client scope applies only if user is permitted to use it.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 case-confusion tests against brokered usernames, Keycloak has a provider setting 'Case-sensitive username'. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating users. The fuzzer MUST treat Admin vs admin collapsing as configuration-driven when this setting is off, and only flag unexpected merges when case-sensitive username is enabled or when comparing non-username identifiers.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity broker general configuration: Case-sensitive username setting.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 multi-organization identity tests using the organization scope, requesting scope=organization without an alias maps a single organization only if the user belongs to exactly one organization; otherwise Keycloak prompts for organization selection. The fuzzer MUST use organization:<alias> or organization:* for deterministic tests involving multi-org memberships.
oidc_jwt.source: Mapping organization claims: organization scope formats and behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 multi-tab or concurrent browser-flow tests, Keycloak authentication sessions expire after the login timeout (30 minutes by default) and other tabs may automatically restart authentication after one tab completes login. The fuzzer MUST distinguish session-expiry or auto-restart behavior from state-swap or code-injection vulnerabilities.
oidc_jwt.source: Authentication sessions documentation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary OIDC bearer access tokens, Keycloak documentation does not claim jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for bearer tokens. Stateless reuse of the same bearer token within its lifetime is expected unless holder-of-key mechanisms such as mTLS or DPoP are configured. The fuzzer MUST NOT flag simple bearer-token replay as a vulnerability by default.
oidc_jwt.source: Compromised tokens guidance and holder-of-key token documentation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests involving refresh tokens, Keycloak supports both refresh token rotation and no rotation depending on realm settings and client policies. The fuzzer MUST determine whether 'Revoke Refresh Token' or suppress-refresh-token-rotation policy is configured before interpreting refresh-token reuse as a bug or expected behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows: Refresh token rotation and suppress-refresh-token-rotation client policy.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: Hashing iterations password policy uses -1 as a sentinel meaning 'use the default iteration count for the selected hashing algorithm', not literal negative iterations. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret -1 as disablement or zero-cost hashing.
oidc_jwt.source: Password policies: Hashing iterations default value is -1 using algorithm defaults.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 to mean 'always re-authenticate before password update', not 'use default' or 'disable'. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as strictest enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Password policies: Maximum Authentication Age value 0 semantics.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 to disable the realm or client session-count check, not to enforce zero sessions. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat 0 as deny-all.
oidc_jwt.source: User session limits documentation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn timeout uses 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not literal immediate expiry. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume zero means instant timeout.
oidc_jwt.source: WebAuthn policy: Timeout default value 0 semantics.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration uses 0 to mean the old secret is immediately removed during client secret rotation. The fuzzer MUST distinguish this from default behavior and avoid assuming overlap when value is 0.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Secret Rotation documentation.
